 Food pantry leaders weigh in on new proposed change to SNAP, gear up for Thanksgiving season
 Garrett Chan News10NBC 
 --> 
 ROCHESTER, N.Y. — Food pantries in the Rochester region are preparing for one of their busiest times of the year as Thanksgiving and the holiday season approach. 
 Pantry leaders say Thanksgiving is coming as many families are struggling with the effects of inflation and high gas prices. It also comes amid some changes to the SNAP food assistance program and a proposed change to who automatically qualifies. 
 While food pantries are feeling the effects of higher food costs, support from partners like Foodlink and Wegmans has helped keep supplies steady. Foodlink, which stores and distributes millions of pounds of food to its partners across the 12-county region, is in the middle of its annual Check Out Hunger campaign to collect donations from Wegmans shoppers. 
 Leaders at the People’s Pantry and Rochester Hope North Clinton Food Pantry say they’re able to meet the demand for fresh produce and meat for now and hope to keep up with needs through the holiday season. 
 “If there’s not a lot of free meats available or low-cost meats, I’m feeling it then. My monthly bill is feeling it then if I have to buy those kinds of things,” said Charyleah Cordone, executive director of People’s Pantry.
 “We are spending more money, but then we’re going to our donors and saying, hey, could you help us out a little bit? Everybody is so wonderful about that,” said Dawn Burdick, executive director of Rochester Hope North Clinton Food Pantry.
 Proposed change to SNAP eligibility
 Last week, the U.S. Department of Agriculture announced a proposal to change SNAP eligibility requirements, which could put more pressure on local food pantries.
 Executive directors at the People’s Pantry and Rochester Hope North Clinton Food Pantry said they are not in favor of more cuts during a time when thousands in the region rely on benefits to keep up with higher food costs. They said they are making sure they have volunteers and resources from Foodlink ready in case the changes take effect. The USDA proposal would stop automatic eligibility for food stamps for households receiving cash under the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program.
 “Although some of them have talked a little bit about their benefits have been cut a little bit. I am working more with the Rochester Works program, though. The able-bodied people that have to go out and either do a job or volunteer,” Cordone said.
 “It’s been proven that also that SNAP, that the money that you spend on SNAP helps the economy in general. like if you’re purchasing thing at the store, they have revenue, they employ people. and so it does have a trickle down effect,” Burdick said.
 If the proposal goes through, the USDA estimates more than 6 million people could lose SNAP benefits by 2029. In Monroe County, about 100,000 people rely on SNAP. Both food pantry directors said they already saw an increase in demand when new federal work requirements and SNAP food restriction waivers took effect in February.
 The People’s Pantry and Rochester Hope North Clinton Food Pantry are also looking for volunteers this time of year.
